advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In service-user.sh, say in the parse-failure error that Gerrit has already rotated the bot token and SSM is stale (rerun required), or parse the token more tolerantly (e.g. pick the 'New password:' line from multi-line output) so a harmless format change doesn't lock out the bot
evidence: infra/gerrit/service-user.sh:62-66: case "$TOKEN" in "" | *[!A-Za-z0-9+/=._~-]*) echo "service-user: unexpected --generate-http-password output (value not printed)" >&2; exit 1
infra/gerrit/service-user.sh:73: printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | aws ssm put-parameter (only reached after the check passes)

Before this change TOKEN came from `openssl rand -hex 32` before any Gerrit call, so the value written to Gerrit was always known and could be stored in SSM. The output format is now version-dependent and appears nowhere in the repo except a test stub (search for 'generate-http-password').
advisory.finding: service-user.sh deletes the bot's default token and has Gerrit generate a new one before it checks the output. If the output isn't a single 'New password: <token>' line (an extra or deprecation line, a different prefix in another Gerrit version, a trailing space), the script exits 1. By then Gerrit holds a new token nobody captured and SSM still has the old, deleted one, so the review bot is locked out until the script is rerun. The error message doesn't say the token was already rotated.
scenarios: A Gerrit upgrade changes or deprecates the --generate-http-password stdout (e.g. prints a warning line or 'New token:'): the rotation run exits 1 after the server-side rotation and the bot starts failing with 401s against the SSM token.
An operator reads 'unexpected output' as 'nothing changed' and doesn't rerun, leaving review-bot auth broken.
advisory.suggested_fix: Pick the token line with a builtin loop, e.g. `while IFS= read -r l; do case $l in 'New password: '*) TOKEN=${l#New password: };; esac; done <<<"$generated"`. In the failure branch, print: "service-user: Gerrit token for '$BOT_USER' was rotated but the new value could not be parsed; SSM ${SSM_TOKEN_PARAM} is now stale — the bot cannot authenticate until this is rerun".

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fail-closed case for prefix-less output with only allowed characters (e.g. generated="oops") and make service-user.sh require the 'New password: ' prefix, or document that bare output is deliberately accepted
evidence: infra/gerrit/service-user.sh:55: "token reaches no local argv. Fail closed on any other shape: the value check also"
infra/gerrit/service-user.sh:59: TOKEN="${generated#New password: }" — if the prefix is absent, this strip does nothing and the raw output becomes TOKEN
infra/gerrit/service-user.sh:63: "" | *[!A-Za-z0-9+/=._~-]*) — the only rejection is for empty output or disallowed characters; a missing prefix is never checked

tests/scripts/test_operator_credential_argv.py:131: ["", "New password:", f"New password: {GENERATED} extra", "New password: a&b", "oops\\x"] — the prefix-less case contains a backslash, so it fails the character check, not a prefix check
Example input: generated="oops" (or a bare token like GENERATED with no prefix). The script would exit 0 and write 'oops' to SSM as the bot token, and no test would catch it.
advisory.finding: The fail-closed test never covers generator output that lacks the 'New password: ' prefix but uses only allowed characters, and service-user.sh accepts such output. The script comment promises it will 'Fail closed on any other shape'. The only prefix-less case in the test ('oops\x') is rejected solely because of the backslash, so the missing-prefix check is never exercised.
scenarios: A different Gerrit version, or a wrapper, prints a one-word status or a bare token on stdout. That value is stored in SSM and rendered into webhooks.config as the bot token, and the bot is then locked out.
advisory.suggested_fix: In service-user.sh, before stripping the prefix, add `case "$generated" in "New password: "*) ;; *) echo "service-user: unexpected --generate-http-password output (value not printed)" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac`. Then add "oops" and GENERATED (bare) to the parametrize list in test_service_user_fails_closed_on_unexpected_generator_output.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a service-user test where the ssh stub prints 'New password: <token>\r' and assert aws-stdin equals the token without the CR
evidence: tests/scripts/test_operator_credential_argv.py:84: the default generated is f"New password: {GENERATED}" with no \r, and no parametrized case adds one
advisory.finding: The new step that strips a trailing carriage return from the generated token has no test. No case feeds 'New password: <token>\r' through the ssh stub to check that SSM and the rendered template get the token without the CR.
scenarios: If the CR strip is removed or reordered, a token ending in \r falls outside the allowed character set. Rotation over a CRLF-producing ssh session would then fail, and no test would detect it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Parametrize test_service_user_keeps_the_token_out_of_every_argv (or add a sibling test) with generated=f"New password: {GENERATED}\r" and assert (rec / "aws-stdin").read_text() == GENERATED.
